messages:
maria: Heads-up: seeing a big latency spike from private-vpc eu-west-1 around 09:12 UTC. 99p gen latency jumped ~120ms -> ~1.2s on /v1/generate. Throughput dropped on our dedicated pool d-42.
ajay: saw the same. GPU queues growing but host CPU looks fine. Opening pprof and tcpdump now.
sophia: logs show TCP retransmits and a bunch of ICMP 'frag needed' messages. Could be MTU/PMTUD issue. Any firewall changes overnight?
liam: no firewall rules changed in the app plane, but infra pushed an egress ACL prune at 02:30 to a subset of VPCs. rolling config? :eyes:
maria: packet capture from worker-7 attached. shows ICMP frag-needed and MSS differences:
```
08:12:15.123456 IP 10.0.7.5 > 3.120.45.2: ICMP frag-needed, mtu 1400
08:12:15.123460 IP 10.0.7.5.50123 > 13.32.1.8.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1450, ack 1, win 29200
```
ajay: interesting. runtime kernel selection fell back to a simpler network path earlier today (we toggled kernel heuristic last week). that fallback doesn't handle fragment reassembly and batching interplay as well. we've seen regressions under egress jitter when `kv-shared` vs `batched-kernel` switches.
sophia: KV cache miss rate also spiked ~3x at the same time in metrics (kv_cache.miss_rate). suspecting retransmits trigger more synchronous fallbacks in the batching code path.
liam: noisy neighbor signal: NAT conntrack on the fronting NAT was near full. `conntrack -L | wc -l` ~120k on a device with default 128k. might be a tenant blasting outbound flows.
nina: ops-bot alerted NAT fd exhaustion at 09:07: `conntrack: table full, dropping packet` — saw alerts for nat-prod-5. :fire:
maria: note: we shipped a batching heuristic tweak yesterday that increased max batch delay to 45ms for larger models. that increases concurrent inflight connections per worker and could amplify conntrack usage.
ajay: triage plan: 1) identify and throttle offending tenant on NAT policer, 2) rollback runtime batching heuristic for eu-west-1 (canary), 3) increase conntrack table on NATs as stopgap, 4) clamp MSS on worker ENIs to 1400 to avoid relying on ICMP.
sophia: perf profile shows time spent in `tcp_sendmsg` and `ip_fragment`. `perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid>` indicates kernel cycles in networking stack increased when we were on fallback kernel. also see more time in our `batch_dispatch` when misses spike.
liam: I'm rolling netscaler ACL rollback to pre-02:30 and adding iptables MSS clamp on the forward path: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360` for now.
nina: bumped conntrack to 256k on nat-prod-5. watching.
maria: toggling runtime flag `batch_delay_ms` back from 45 -> 25 on a 10% canary in eu-west-1.
deploy-bot: deployment started: canary rollback batch_delay_ms -> 25 on eu-west-1 (10%) — build r2419.
ajay: canary results: workers with rollback dropped 99p latency to ~140ms and throughput recovered ~15% vs affected pool. good signal.
sophia: plan to run synthetic load to validate KV cache behavior under lower batch delay: `tools/loadgen --model t-7b --qps 200` and capture `kv_cache.*` metrics + pprof.
maria: long-term actions: improve kernel selection logic to prefer batched-kernel when we detect PMTUD/ICMP frag-needed patterns, add batching heuristics that consider observed egress stability, and add NAT autoscaling/policing per customer to avoid one tenant taking down conntrack.
liam: also propose adding e2e tests for private deployments: simulate MTU=1400 and conntrack saturation in CI so this regresses earlier.
nina: filing tickets: INFRA-842 (NAT autoscale), INFRA-843 (egress MTU regression tests), RUNTIME-129 (batching rollback guard + kernel selection tweak). assigning owners.
maria: thanks all — I'll start the incident writeup and add metric graphs. will update postmortem when metrics stabilize. :thumbsup:
